content.text:
I've submitted index 122 (Bi 0.55, Cu 0.20, V 0.26) as the best composition. It gave 7.6e-7 A, the highest of the three I measured. I don't know how it compares with the best in the library, because I only measured 3 of the 296 compositions.

- **XRD (3 of 5 used):** I scanned 286, 161 and 10, all with low Cu. All three show the strongest peak of monoclinic BiVO₄ (Q ≈ 2.035 Å⁻¹), a known photoanode material. 286 had the fewest extra peaks. 161 and 10 had extra peaks I couldn't identify; at 10 they may come from a copper vanadate.
- **Photocurrent (all 3 measurements used):**
  - 286 (Bi 0.43): 1.0e-7 A
  - 161 (Bi 0.47): 1.6e-7 A
  - 122 (Bi 0.55): 7.6e-7 A

  Photocurrent rose as the Bi fraction went up, so I spent the last measurement further in that direction.

**What's still open:** the trend was still climbing at 122, so compositions with even more Bi might do better. Examples are 157 and 180 (Bi about 0.60–0.62, Cu about 0.20); I didn't measure them. I also didn't sample the Cu-rich or V-rich parts of the library at all. I left 2 XRD scans unused, and they wouldn't have changed which compositions I measured.
